message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are earned by being the first to empty your hand in each round. | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (standard Uno).
• Each player draws 7 cards.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card (Skip, Reverse, Draw Two, Wild, or Wild Draw Four), follow its effect immediately. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a Reverse card changes direction). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches either:
• the color of the top discard card,
• the number/symbol of the top discard card,
• or a Wild card (any color).
After playing, the card’s effect (if any) takes place immediately. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you can be challenged.) | | **Drawing** | If you cannot play a card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise the turn ends. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, you must say “Uno!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards remaining in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip, Reverse, Draw Two = 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each. | | **Winning the Game** | First player to reach the target score (usually 500) wins. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep an eye on the discard pile** – you can anticipate what cards opponents might play. 2. **Use Wild Draw Four wisely** – it’s powerful but risky if you’re caught. 3. **Plan your “Uno” call** – you can’t play a card after calling “Uno”; you must wait until your next turn. 4. **Keep the draw pile topped** – if it runs out, shuffle the discard pile (except the top card) to form a new draw pile. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
